newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard says wants budget passed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard says wants budget passed.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday he did not want to hold an early election, but warned the government was anxious to have its entire budget legislation passed in the upper house of parliament, the Senate.

"We are not spoiling for another election, we're not spoiling for a double dissolution, but ultimately we'll do what is necessary to get our programmes through," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
Howard said the Australian public had given its support to the government's budget measures at the March 2 election and as a result, the Senate should not delay the budgetary process.

"I don't think the public wants to be racing off to an early new election, but equally I don't think the public wants important elements of the programme of the government delayed indefinitely," he said.

Treasurer Peter Costello raised the possibility of an early election last Thursday after the Senate substantially amended the government's social security bill on Tuesday, costing the budget an extra A$400 million over the next four years.
The government can call an early election if the Senate rejects a bill twice.

Costello said the government would ask the Senate to reconsider its vote this week and if it failed to reconsider, the government would re-introduce the bill in three months' time as it is entitled to under the constitution.
Howard said the government remained hopeful it could negotiate with the minor parties in the Senate on contentious budget measures in order to have them passed.
"We are prepared to talk to the minor parties in the Senate," he said.
"We're prepared to be reasonable, but not surrender important principles."
The government needs two additional votes to pass any legislation in the Senate, where it does not have a majority.
